name: Heritage Village (Calle Crisologo)
tagline: The cobblestoned colonial heart of Vigan
description: Vigan's UNESCO-listed core, where cobblestoned Calle Crisologo runs between ancestral bahay-na-bato mansions and kalesa carriages clop past souvenir stalls and cafes. Atmospheric and central, it is the most touristy and photogenic corner of the whole town.
bestFor: History lovers and photographers who want to live amid the heritage
pros: Cafes and dining on the doorstep

name: Plaza Salcedo and Plaza Burgos
tagline: Civic plazas by the grand cathedral
description: The ceremonial centre around twin plazas and the Vigan Cathedral, home to the evening dancing-fountain show, street-food stalls and local gatherings. Lively yet dignified, it blends everyday town life with heritage grandeur just steps from Calle Crisologo.
bestFor: Nomads wanting plaza life, evening events and easy access to everything
pros: Evening fountain show and food stalls

name: Vigan City Proper (near the public market)
tagline: Everyday working town by the market
description: The practical, workaday side of Vigan around the public market and main commercial streets, where residents shop, run errands and catch tricycles. Less polished than the heritage core but cheaper, authentic and handy for daily needs and cheap local eats.
bestFor: Budget nomads who value cheap living and everyday convenience over polish

name: Bantay (across the river)
description: A calmer residential town just across the Mestizo River, known for its landmark bell tower and hilltop views. Greener and more laid-back than central Vigan, it offers cheaper, quieter living while remaining a short tricycle hop from the heritage core.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting calm, space and lower costs near the centre
pros: Scenic bell tower and hill views
